items.stem: Which of the following is part of the definition of an intangible asset under IAS 38?

options.text: An identifiable non-monetary asset without physical substance
options.rationale: Correct: an intangible asset is identifiable, non-monetary and lacks physical substance.
Monetary receivables are not intangible assets.
Equipment has physical substance and is not intangible.

options.text: Any expenditure management hopes will generate profit
options.rationale: Mere hopeful expenditure is not an intangible asset.

items.explanation: Correct: an intangible asset is identifiable, non-monetary and lacks physical substance.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO costs are expensed rather than capitalised under IAS 38? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Expenditure in the research phase of an internal project
options.rationale: Correct: research costs are expensed as incurred.
Correct: internally generated goodwill is not recognised and such costs are expensed.

options.text: Development expenditure that meets all six capitalisation criteria
options.rationale: Qualifying development costs are capitalised, not expensed.

options.text: The purchase price of a separately acquired patent
options.rationale: A separately acquired patent is capitalised.

items.explanation: Correct: research costs are expensed as incurred.

items.stem: A company wants to recognise its internally generated brand, built through years of marketing, as an intangible asset. Why is this generally not permitted?

options.text: Internally generated brands cannot be distinguished from the cost of developing the business as a whole, so they are not recognised
options.rationale: Correct: internally generated brands and goodwill are not recognised.

options.text: Brands never provide future economic benefits
options.rationale: Brands can provide benefits; the issue is reliable separate measurement.

options.text: Only tangible assets can be recognised
options.rationale: Intangibles can be recognised; internally generated brands specifically cannot.

options.text: Brands must always be expensed because marketing is illegal to capitalise by law
options.rationale: There is no such legal rule; the reason is the recognition criteria.

items.explanation: Correct: internally generated brands and goodwill are not recognised.
